inputs.original_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden did the right thing by signing Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, which now requires new registered voters to prove they are United States citizens before casting ballots in state elections. This restores the basic order our republic depends on, making sure only those with a legitimate stake in America get to shape its future. Progressive institutions have spent years trying to weaken citizenship standards and erode national sovereignty in the name of inclusion, but leaders like Rhoden are pushing back with the authority and tradition that built this country. It reinforces personal responsibility by treating the vote as a serious duty reserved for Americans, not outsiders, and protects the cultural continuity that keeps our society stable and focused on the families and communities who sustain it.
inputs.modified_text: South Dakota Governor Larry Rhoden took the right step by signing Senate Bill 175 on Thursday, now requiring new registered voters to prove they are United States citizens before casting ballots in state elections. This kind of action upholds the basic order and sovereignty our republic depends on, ensuring only those with a genuine stake in America get to decide its direction. Progressive institutions have pushed for years to dilute citizenship standards and weaken national boundaries under the cover of inclusion, but leaders like Rhoden are restoring the authority and tradition that built this country. It demands personal responsibility by treating the vote as a serious duty for Americans, not something handed to outsiders, and it defends the cultural continuity that keeps our families and communities strong and stable.
